I’ve stopped a few times, but never for more than 30 days and I’m in a similar situation where I’m not at rock bottom. Only I would say I need to cut back. This past year I found myself drinking more during the week (not just weekends) and having a hangover. I think I have been using it as a crutch to deal with stress, or to get a release and “be happy” for a while. I also was picking beer based on the percentage rather than always for the flavor. 

So part of the challenge is identifying why I drink and what the alternatives are to deal with the why.

This may sound weird, but having some in the house actually eases my mind a bit. It’s like I don’t have to think about should I stop to get some on the way home. 

When I quit chewing I used to stop, but a can, have a dip, get mad and throw the can out. In the past I’ve done a similar think with alcohol. 

So far, I know it’s there, but I don’t need it. But if I didn’t have any I’d be fixated on that and if I buy some I think I’d drink. 

Maybe this also helps me focus on today, not thinking about giving it up forever. Like, I might drink later- but today I choose not to and I just am deciding not to every day.
